items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: Taught me how to use the hi-hat listening to him... So I use a jazz technique in a big band, so I pull from him, definitely a master

ctx.x: Well I heard them, in oh gosh it must have been probably around ‘65 I think. Would that make sense? They were together then right? At the Eastman School of Music. And that was a good one. But I just remember how unassuming Desmond especially. You know I mean he looked like a banker or something. But he had that sense of, if you could sit down and write out a perfect solo, he already played it.

Yeah definitely a lyricist, a wonderful, wonderful player. Something about Paul Desmond to this day you can hear a saxophone and you know right away. Something that you don’t hear from the younger players today. Everybody is tending to sound the same. When you hear Phil Woods you know it’s Phil Woods. Paul Desmond, you know it’s him. Joe Morello you know it’s him. Tony. Drummers tend, and other musicians too tend to want to sound all alike. You know it’s probably the fault of sound men, they have one sound,…
Good words. In fact you anticipated my wrap up question here, was if you had words of advice for upcoming students, I think you did but would you add anything to that?
